1638.subject: Physics
1638.text:
Assertion : Magnetic susceptibillity is a pure number.
Reason : The value of magnetic susceptibility for vacuum is one.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
1638.sol:
Magnetic susceptibility $\left(\chi_{\mathrm{m}}\right)$ is defined as the ratio of the intensity $(I)$ of magnetisation to the magnetic intensity $(H)$ of the magnetising field, that is
$\chi_m=\frac{I}{H}$
It is a pure number, because $I and H$ have the same unit. Its value for vacuum is zero as there can be no magnetisation in vacuum.

Here, $u=-25 \mathrm{~cm} v=-1 \mathrm{~m}=-100 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{-100}+\frac{1}{25}=\frac{3}{100}$
or $f=\frac{100}{3} \mathrm{~cm}=\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~m}$
Therefore, required power,
$P=\frac{1}{f(\mathrm{~m})}=\frac{1}{1 / 3}$
$P=3 \mathrm{D}$

4304.text: The correct order of acidic character of the following is:
4304.sol:
The acidity is directly proportional to the tendency of the hydrogen donor. It depends upon the bond dissociation enthalpy of the $X - H$ bond where $X$ is $Te, Se, S \text{ and } O$. Down the group the bond dissociation energy of hydrides decreases and the acidic strength increases.

Hence, the correct order of acidic character of the given hydrides is ${H}_{2}Te > {H}_{2}Se > {H}_{2}S > {H}_{2}O$.

10606.text: The probability that a person goes to college by car is $\frac{1}{5}$; by bus $\frac{2}{5}$ and by train is $\frac{3}{5}$ respectively. The probabilities that he reaches the college late if he takes car, bus, train are $\frac{2}{7}, \frac{4}{7}$ and $\frac{1}{7}$ respectively. If he reaches the college in time, the probability that he traveled by car is
10606.sol:
Let $\mathrm{C}=$ The event that person goes by car
$\mathrm{B}=$ The event that person goes by bus
$\mathrm{T}=$ The event that person goes by train and $L=$ The event that person reach as college late
Now, $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{C})=\frac{1}{5}, \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})=\frac{2}{5}, \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{T})=\frac{3}{5}\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{C}}\right)=\frac{2}{7}, \mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{B}}\right)=\frac{4}{7}, \mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}}{\mathrm{T}}\right)=\frac{1}{7} \\ & \text{ and } \mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{C}}\right)=\frac{5}{7}, \mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{B}}\right)=\frac{3}{7}, \mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{L}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{T}}\right)=\frac{6}{7}\end{aligned}$
So, $P\left(\frac{C}{L^{\prime}}\right)=\frac{P\left(\frac{L^{\prime}}{C}\right) P(C)}{P\left(\frac{L^{\prime}}{C}\right) P(C)+P\left(\frac{L^{\prime}}{B}\right) P(B)+P\left(\frac{L^{\prime}}{T}\right) P(T)}=\frac{\frac{5}{7} \times \frac{1}{5}}{\frac{5}{7} \times \frac{1}{5}+\frac{3}{7} \times \frac{2}{5}+\frac{6}{7} \times \frac{3}{5}}=\frac{5}{5+6+18}=\frac{5}{29}$

\begin{array}{cccc}$& White & Black & Red \\

Hence, $P\left(B_1\right)=\frac{2}{6}$
Similary, $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{B}_2\right)=\frac{2}{6}$ and $\mathrm{P}\left(\mathrm{B}_3\right)=\frac{2}{6}$
For box $\mathrm{B}_1$ :
Total number of balls $=5$
No. of red balls $=2\therefore$ Probability of red ball $=\frac{2}{5} \Rightarrow P\left(\frac{R}{B_1}\right)=\frac{2}{5}$
Similarly, $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{B}_2}\right)=\frac{4}{9}$ and $\mathrm{P}\left(\frac{\mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{B}_3}\right)=\frac{2}{9}$ Now, the required probability is
$P\left(\frac{B_2}{R}\right)=\frac{P\left(\frac{R}{B_2}\right) P\left(B_2\right)}{P\left(\frac{R}{B_1}\right) P\left(B_1\right)+P\left(\frac{R}{B_2}\right) P\left(B_2\right)+P\left(\frac{R}{B_3}\right) P\left(B_3\right)}=\frac{\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{2}{6}}{\frac{2}{6} \times \frac{2}{5}+\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{2}{6}+\frac{2}{9} \times \frac{2}{6}}=\frac{5}{12}$

Given statements,
I. In $\triangle A B C$, if c=6 and $\cos C=-\frac{11}{25}$.
Then, $\sin C=\sqrt{1-\frac{121}{625}}=\sqrt{\frac{625-121}{625}}$
=$\sqrt{\frac{504}{25}}=\frac{6 \sqrt{14}}{25} \because \quad \frac{c}{\sin C}=2 R \Rightarrow R=\frac{6}{2 \times \frac{6 \sqrt{14}}{25}}=\frac{25}{2 \sqrt{14}}$ So, statement (I) is true.
II. In $\triangle A B C$, if $a=3, b=4, c=6$, then $\begin{aligned}& \cos C=\frac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2 a b}=\frac{9+16-36}{2 \times 3 \times 4}=-\frac{11}{24}\\
\because & \cos C < 0
\end{aligned} $\therefore \quad \triangle A B C$ is a obtuse angled triangle.
So, Statement (II) is false.$

19743.subject: Chemistry
19743.text: According to Molecular orbital theory, which of the following is correct with respect to bond order?
options: Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ and $\text{O}_2^+$ is less than $\text{O}_2$
Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than $\text{N}_2$ while that of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{O}_2$.
Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ and $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{N}_2$
Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than $\text{O}_2$ while that of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{O}_2$.
19743.sol:
Bond order is calculated as $\dfrac{N_b - N_a}{2}$, where $N_b$ is the number of bonding electrons and $N_a$ is the number of antibonding electrons.

For $\text{N}_2$ ($14$ electrons), the molecular orbital configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2$
Bond order = $\dfrac{10 - 4}{2} = 3$

For $\text{N}_2^+$ ($13$ electrons), the configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^1$
Bond order = $\dfrac{9 - 4}{2} = 2.5$
Thus, the bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than that of $\text{N}_2$.

For $\text{O}_2$ ($16$ electrons), the configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}{}^1 \pi^{*}_{2p_y}{}^1$
Bond order = $\dfrac{10 - 6}{2} = 2$

For $\text{O}_2^+$ ($15$ electrons), the configuration is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}{}^1$
Bond order = $\dfrac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5$
Thus, the bond order of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than that of $\text{O}_2$.

Answer: Bond order of $\text{N}_2^+$ is less than $\text{N}_2$ while that of $\text{O}_2^+$ is more than $\text{O}_2$.

20753.subject: Chemistry
20753.text: Calculate the difference between $C_{p}$ and $C_{V}$ for 10 moles of an ideal gas
20753.sol:
For an ideal gas, the relationship between molar heat capacities at constant pressure $C_{p,m}$ and constant volume $C_{V,m}$ is given by Mayer's relation: $C_{p,m} - C_{V,m} = R$, where $R$ is the universal gas constant.

For $n$ moles of an ideal gas, the total heat capacities are $C_{p} = n C_{p,m}$ and $C_{V} = n C_{V,m}$.

Therefore, the difference is $C_{p} - C_{V} = n(C_{p,m} - C_{V,m}) = nR$.

Given $n = 10$ moles and $R = 8.314$ J/(mol K), the difference is:

$C_{p} - C_{V} = 10 \times 8.314$ J/K = $83.14$ J/K.

Answer: 83.14 J/K

21575.subject: Mathematics
21575.sol:
Let $I = \int \dfrac{2^{x}}{\sqrt{1-4^{x}}} dx$.

Rewrite the integral as $I = \int \dfrac{2^{x}}{\sqrt{1-(2^{x})^{2}}} dx$.

Substitute $u = 2^{x}$. Then $du = 2^{x} \ln 2 \, dx$, which implies $2^{x} dx = \dfrac{du}{\ln 2}$.

Substituting these into the integral gives $I = \int \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}} \cdot \dfrac{du}{\ln 2}$.

$I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 2} \int \dfrac{du}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}$.

Using the standard integral formula $\int \dfrac{du}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}} = \sin^{-1} u + C$, we get $I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 2} \sin^{-1} u + C$.

Substituting back $u = 2^{x}$, we obtain $I = \dfrac{1}{\ln 2} \sin^{-1} 2^{x} + C$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\log 2} \sin ^{-1} 2^{x}+C$

22223.subject: Mathematics
22223.text: Find the general solution of $\sin 2 x+\cos x=0$.
22223.sol:
The given equation is $\sin 2x + \cos x = 0$.

Using the double angle identity $\sin 2x = 2 \sin x \cos x$, the equation becomes $2 \sin x \cos x + \cos x = 0$.

Factoring out $\cos x$, we get $\cos x (2 \sin x + 1) = 0$.

This implies either $\cos x = 0$ or $2 \sin x + 1 = 0$.

For $\cos x = 0$, the general solution is $x = (2n + 1) \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, which can also be written as $n \pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

For $2 \sin x + 1 = 0$, we have $\sin x = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $\sin x = -\sin \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \sin(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}) = \sin(\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6}) = \sin(\dfrac{7\pi}{6})$, the general solution is $x = n \pi + (-1)^n (-\dfrac{\pi}{6})$ or $x = n \pi + (-1)^n \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$.

Comparing these results with the given options, the solution set is $x = n \pi + (-1)^n \dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ or $x = (2n \pm 1) \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Answer: $n \pi+(-1)^n \dfrac{7 \pi}{6}$ or $(2 n \pm 1) \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

23615.subject: Physics
23615.text: If $R$ and $C$ denote resistance and capacitance of a material, then the dimension of $C R$ will be :
23615.sol:
The dimension of resistance $R$ is given by $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$. Since $V = \dfrac{W}{q}$, we have $R = \dfrac{W}{Iq} = \dfrac{[ML^2T^{-2}]}{[A][AT]} = [ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}]$.

The dimension of capacitance $C$ is given by $C = \dfrac{q}{V}$. Since $V = \dfrac{W}{q}$, we have $C = \dfrac{q^2}{W} = \dfrac{[AT]^2}{[ML^2T^{-2}]} = [M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2]$.

The product $CR$ has dimensions $[M^{-1}L^{-2}T^4A^2] \times [ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}] = [M^{1-1}L^{2-2}T^{4-3}A^{2-2}] = [M^0L^0T^1]$.

Thus, the dimension of $CR$ is $[T]$, which corresponds to $[M^0L^0T]$.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{~L}^0 \mathrm{~T}\right]$

23634.subject: Physics
23634.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the slit separation is 1.5 mm. The setup is illuminated simultaneously by light of wavelengths 6000 Å and 8000 Å. The screen is placed at a distance of 1.5 m from the slits. It is observed that at a certain point P on the screen which is 4.8mm from the central maximum, fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide. Which of the following options are correct?
options: Light of wavelength 6000 Å produces a dark fringe and light of wavelength 8000 Å produces a bright fringe at P
Light of wavelength 6000 Å produces a bright fringe and light of wavelength 8000 Å produces a dark fringe at P
Light of wavelength 6000 Å and light of wavelength 8000 Å both produce a dark fringe at P
Light of wavelength 6000 Å and light of wavelength 8000 Å both produce a bright fringe at P
23634.sol:
The path difference at point P is given by $\Delta x = \dfrac{y d}{D}$.

Substituting the given values:
$\Delta x = \dfrac{4.8 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3}}{1.5} = 4.8 \times 10^{-6}$ m.

For wavelength $\lambda_1 = 6000 \times 10^{-10}$ m $= 6 \times 10^{-7}$ m, the order of the fringe is:
$n_1 = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\lambda_1} = \dfrac{4.8 \times 10^{-6}}{6 \times 10^{-7}} = 8$
Since $n_1$ is an integer, a bright fringe is formed at P by $\lambda_1$.

For wavelength $\lambda_2 = 8000 \times 10^{-10}$ m $= 8 \times 10^{-7}$ m, the order of the fringe is:
$n_2 = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\lambda_2} = \dfrac{4.8 \times 10^{-6}}{8 \times 10^{-7}} = 6$
Since $n_2$ is also an integer, a bright fringe is formed at P by $\lambda_2$.

Thus, both wavelengths produce a bright fringe at P.

Answer: Light of wavelength 6000 Å and light of wavelength 8000 Å both produce a bright fringe at P

26312.subject: Physics
26312.text: A hollow, right circular cone of base radius $R$ and height $h$, with its tip at the origin is rotating about the $Z$-axis with an angular velocity $\omega$, as shown in the figure. The cone carries a total charge $Q$ uniformly distributed on its curved surface. The magnitude of magnetic field at a point $(0, 0, z)$, where $z \gg R$ and $z \gg h$, is $\dfrac{n\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{Q R^2 \omega}{z^3}$. The value of $n$ is:
26312.sol:
For a point on the axis at a distance $z \gg R$ and $z \gg h$, the rotating cone can be considered as a magnetic dipole. The magnetic field on the axis of a dipole is given by:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{2M}{z^3}$

where $M$ is the magnetic dipole moment of the cone.

To find $M$, consider an elemental ring on the cone at a vertical distance $y$ from the origin, with vertical thickness $dy$. The radius of this ring is $r = \dfrac{R}{h}y$ and its slant length is $dl = \dfrac{\sqrt{R^2+h^2}}{h}dy$.

The surface charge density of the cone is $\sigma = \dfrac{Q}{\pi R \sqrt{R^2+h^2}}$.

The charge on the elemental ring is:

$dq = \sigma (2\pi r dl) = \dfrac{Q}{\pi R \sqrt{R^2+h^2}} \left(2\pi \dfrac{R}{h}y \dfrac{\sqrt{R^2+h^2}}{h}dy\right) = \dfrac{2Q}{h^2}y dy$

The current due to the rotation of this ring is:

$dI = \dfrac{dq}{T} = \dfrac{dq \omega}{2\pi} = \dfrac{Q\omega}{\pi h^2}y dy$

The magnetic moment of this elemental ring is:

$dM = dI (\pi r^2) = \left(\dfrac{Q\omega}{\pi h^2}y dy\right) \pi \left(\dfrac{R}{h}y\right)^2 = \dfrac{Q\omega R^2}{h^4}y^3 dy$

Integrating from $y = 0$ to $y = h$, the total magnetic moment is:

$M = \int_{0}^{h} \dfrac{Q\omega R^2}{h^4}y^3 dy = \dfrac{Q\omega R^2}{h^4} \left[\dfrac{y^4}{4}\right]_{0}^{h} = \dfrac{Q\omega R^2}{4}$

Alternatively, using the gyromagnetic ratio for a uniform charge distribution, $\dfrac{M}{L_{ang}} = \dfrac{Q}{2m}$. The moment of inertia of a hollow cone is $I = \dfrac{1}{2}mR^2$, so the angular momentum is $L_{ang} = \dfrac{1}{2}mR^2\omega$. Thus, $M = \dfrac{Q}{2m} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}mR^2\omega\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}QR^2\omega$.

Substituting $M$ into the magnetic field formula:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{2}{z^3} \left(\dfrac{1}{4}QR^2\omega\right) = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{QR^2\omega}{2z^3}$

Comparing this with the given expression $B = \dfrac{n\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{QR^2\omega}{z^3}$, we get:

$n = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$

Answer: $0.5$

30214.subject: Chemistry
30214.text: The correct order of reactivity of $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{Br}$ in methanol with the following nucleophiles is $\mathrm{F}^{-}, \mathrm{I}^{-}, \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{O}^{-}$and $\mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{5} \mathrm{O}^{-}$
30214.sol:
In methanol (protic solvent), nucleophilicity is determined by basicity and solvation effects. Smaller ions are heavily solvated by the protic solvent, reducing their effective nucleophilicity.

C₂H₅O⁻ (ethoxide) is the strongest nucleophile as it is less solvated and highly basic.

C₆H₅O⁻ (phenoxide) is weaker due to resonance stabilization by the benzene ring.

F⁻ is highly solvated despite high basicity, reducing its nucleophilicity significantly.

I⁻ is the best nucleophile because it is the largest ion and least solvated in methanol.

The correct order is I⁻ > C₂H₅O⁻ > C₆H₅O⁻ > F⁻.

30253.subject: Chemistry
30253.text: The correct statement regarding nucleophilic substitution reaction in a chiral alkyl halide is ;
options: Retention occurs in ${S}_{N}l$reaction and inversion occurs in ${S}_{N}2$ reaction.
Racemisation occurs in ${S}_{N}l$reaction and retention occurs in ${S}_{N}2$ reaction.
Racemisation occurs in both ${S}_{N}1$ and ${S}_{N}2$ reactions.
Racemisation occurs in ${S}_{N}1$ reaction and inversion occurs in ${S}_{N}2$ reaction.
30253.sol:
In the 1st step of ${S}_{N}1$ mechanism a carbocation is formed which is planar .Therefore the nucleophile can attack the carbocation from both the sides. When a nucleophile attacks the carbocation from the side where initially halogen was there,the product with retention in configuration is produce and when nucleophile attacks the carbocation from backside, the product with inversion in configuration is produce. Hence $50$% of the product will be with retention in configuration and rest $50$% will be with inversion in configuration. This produces a racemic mixture which is optically inactive.

In ${S}_{N}2$ reaction mechanism requires the attack of nucleophile from the back side of the carbon atom. So the product assumes a stereochemical position opposite to the leaving group originally occupied. This is called inversion of configuration.

${S}_{N}1$ – Racemisation

${S}_{N}2$ – Inversion

Hence option D is the answer.

34640.text: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $(1 + \sin x)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (y+1)\cos x = 0$, $y(0) = 0$. If the curve $y = y(x)$ passes through the point $\left(\alpha, \dfrac{-1}{2}\right)$, then a value of $\alpha$ is :
34640.sol:
The given differential equation can be written as:

$(1 + \sin x)dy + (y+1)\cos x dx = 0$

$d((y+1)(1 + \sin x)) = 0$

Integrating both sides:

$(y+1)(1 + \sin x) = C$

Given $y(0) = 0$, substituting $x = 0 and y = 0$:

$(0+1)(1 + \sin 0) = C \Rightarrow C = 1$

The equation of the curve is $(y+1)(1 + \sin x) = 1$

Since the curve passes through $\left(\alpha, \dfrac{-1}{2}\right)$, substituting $x = \alpha$ and $y = \dfrac{-1}{2}$:

$\left(\dfrac{-1}{2} + 1\right)(1 + \sin \alpha) = 1$

$\dfrac{1}{2}(1 + \sin \alpha) = 1$

$1 + \sin \alpha = 2$

$\sin \alpha = 1$

$\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

36798.text: If two vertices of an equilateral triangle are $\mathrm{A}(-a, 0)$ and $B(a, 0), a>0$, and the third vertex C lies above $x$-axis then the equation of the circumcircle of $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$ is :
36798.sol:
Let $\mathrm{C}=(x, y)$
Now, $\mathrm{CA}^2=\mathrm{CB}^2=\mathrm{AB}^2\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow(x+a)^2+y²=(x-a)^2+y²=(2 a)^2 \\
& \Rightarrow x²+2 a x+a²+y²=4 a² \\
& $\text{$ and }x^2-2 a x+a²+y²=4 a²
\end{aligned}

From (i) and (ii), x=0 and $y=\pm \sqrt{3} a$
Since point $\mathrm{C}(x, y)$ lies above the $x$-axis and $a \gt 0$, hence $y=\sqrt{3} a$
\therefore \quad $\mathrm{C}=($0, $\sqrt{3}$a)

Let the equation of circumcircle be

x²+y²+2 g x+2 f y+$\mathrm{C}=$0

Since points A( $-a, 0), \mathrm{B}(a, 0)$ and $\mathrm{C}(0, \sqrt{3} a)$ lie on the circle, therefore

$\begin{aligned}$& a²-2 g a+$\mathrm{C}=$0 \\
& a²+2 g a+$\mathrm{C}=$0
\end{aligned}$ and 3 a^2+2 \sqrt{3} a f+\mathrm{C}=0$
From (iii), (iv), and (v)

g=0, c=-a², f=-$\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}$Hence equation of the circumcircle is

$\begin{aligned}$& x²+y²-$\frac{2 a}{\sqrt{3}}$y-a²=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x²+y²-$\frac{2 \sqrt{3} a y}{3}-$a^2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 x²+3 y²-2 $\sqrt{3}$a y=3 a²
\end{aligned}

36916.text: The value of $3 + \dfrac{1}{4 + \dfrac{1}{3 + \dfrac{1}{4 + \dfrac{1}{3 + \ldots \infty}}}}$ is equal to
36916.sol:
Let $x = 3 + \dfrac{1}{4 + \dfrac{1}{3 + \dfrac{1}{4 + \dfrac{1}{3 + \ldots \infty}}}}$

So, $x = 3 + \dfrac{1}{4 + \dfrac{1}{x}} = 3 + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{4x + 1}{x}}$

$⇒ \left(x - 3\right) = \dfrac{x}{( 4x + 1 )}$

$⇒ ( 4x + 1 ) ( x - 3 ) = x$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} - 12x + x - 3 = x$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} - 12x - 3 = 0$

$x = \dfrac{12 \pm \sqrt{( 12{)}^{2} + 12 \times 4}}{2 \times 4} = \dfrac{12 \pm \sqrt{12 ( 16 )}}{8}$

$= \dfrac{12 \pm 4 \times 2\sqrt{3}}{8} = \dfrac{3 \pm 2\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$x = \dfrac{3}{2} \pm \sqrt{3} = 1 . 5 \pm \sqrt{3} .$

But only positive value is accepted

So, $x = 1 . 5 + \sqrt{3}$

37025.subject: Mathematics
37025.text: Let $\alpha, \alpha + 2, \alpha \in \mathbb{Z}$, be the roots of the quadratic equation $x(x+2) + (x+1)(x+3) + (x+2)(x+4) + \ldots + (x+n-1)(x+n+1) = 4n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $n + \alpha$ is equal to :
37025.sol:
The given equation is:

$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (x+k)(x+k+2) = 4n$

Expanding the terms inside the summation:

$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (x^2 + 2(k+1)x + k(k+2)) = 4n$

Summing each term separately:

$n x^2 + 2x \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (k+1) + \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (k^2 + 2k) = 4n$

Using the standard summation formulas:

$n x^2 + 2x \dfrac{n(n+1)}{2} + \dfrac{(n-1)n(2n-1)}{6} + 2 \dfrac{(n-1)n}{2} = 4n$

$n x^2 + n(n+1)x + \dfrac{n(n-1)(2n+5)}{6} = 4n$

Since $n \in \mathbb{N}$, dividing the entire equation by $n$ gives:

$x^2 + (n+1)x + \dfrac{(n-1)(2n+5)}{6} - 4 = 0$

The roots of this quadratic equation are given as $\alpha$ and $\alpha + 2$.

Using the sum of the roots:

$\alpha + (\alpha + 2) = -(n+1)$

$2\alpha + 2 = -n - 1 \Rightarrow n = -2\alpha - 3$

Using the product of the roots:

$\alpha(\alpha + 2) = \dfrac{(n-1)(2n+5)}{6} - 4$

Substituting $n = -2\alpha - 3$ into the product equation:

$\alpha^2 + 2\alpha = \dfrac{(-2\alpha - 4)(-4\alpha - 1)}{6} - 4$

$6(\alpha^2 + 2\alpha) = 8\alpha^2 + 18\alpha + 4 - 24$

$6\alpha^2 + 12\alpha = 8\alpha^2 + 18\alpha - 20$

$2\alpha^2 + 6\alpha - 20 = 0$

$\alpha^2 + 3\alpha - 10 = 0$

$(\alpha + 5)(\alpha - 2) = 0$

Thus, $\alpha = -5$ or $\alpha = 2$.

If $\alpha = 2$, then $n = -2(2) - 3 = -7$, which is rejected since $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

If $\alpha = -5$, then $n = -2(-5) - 3 = 7$, which is valid.

Therefore, $n + \alpha = 7 + (-5) = 2$.

Answer: $2$

37115.text: Let $f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}k \cdot {x}^{k}, x \in \mathbb{R}$, if $2f\left(2\right) + {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = 119{\left(2\right)}^{n} + 1$ then $n$ is equal to ______.
37115.sol:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{10}k \cdot {x}^{k}, x \in \mathbb{R}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + 2{x}^{2} + 3{x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots \ldots + 10{x}^{10}$

Now let $S = x + 2{x}^{2} + 3{x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots \ldots + 10{x}^{10}$

So, $S \cdot x = {x}^{2} + 2{x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots + 9{x}^{10} + 10{x}^{11}$

Now subtracting above equations we get,

$S\left(1 - x\right) = x + {x}^{2} + {x}^{3} + \ldots \ldots + {x}^{10} - 10{x}^{11}$

$⇒ S\left(1 - x\right) = \dfrac{x\left(1 - {x}^{10}\right)}{1 - x} - 10{x}^{11}$

$⇒ S = \dfrac{x\left(1 - {x}^{10}\right)}{{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{10{x}^{11}}{\left(1 - x\right)} = f\left(x\right)$

Now finding, $f\left(2\right) = 2\left(1 - {2}^{10}\right) + 10 \cdot {2}^{11}$

$⇒ f\left(2\right) = 2 + 18 \cdot {2}^{10}$

Now finding ${f}^{'}\left(x\right)$ we get,

${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 10{x}^{11}}{{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{110{x}^{10}}{1 - x} - \dfrac{10{x}^{10}}{{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{2x\left(1 - {x}^{10}\right)}{{\left(1 - x\right)}^{3}} + \dfrac{1 - {x}^{10}}{{\left(1 - x\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = \dfrac{- 10 \cdot {2}^{11}}{{\left(1 - 2\right)}^{2}} - \dfrac{110 \cdot {2}^{10}}{1 - 2} - \dfrac{10 \cdot {2}^{10}}{{\left(1 - 2\right)}^{2}} + \dfrac{2 \cdot 2 \cdot \left(1 - {2}^{10}\right)}{{\left(1 - 2\right)}^{3}} + \dfrac{1 - {2}^{10}}{{\left(1 - 2\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = - 10 \cdot {2}^{11} + 110 \cdot {2}^{10} - 10 \cdot {2}^{10} - 4\left(1 - {2}^{10}\right) + 1 - {2}^{10}$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(2\right) = 83 \cdot {2}^{10} - 3$

$2f ( 2 ) + {f}^{'} ( 2 ) = 2\left(2 + 18 \cdot {2}^{10}\right) + 83 \cdot {2}^{10} - 3 = 119 ( 2{)}^{10} + 1$

$∴ n = 10$

37963.text: If the mirror image of the point $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$ in the line $\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1}$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right),$ then $14 \left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) is:$
37963.sol:
The given point is $P ( 3, 4, 9 )$.

Let, $Q\left(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\right) be$ the image ofP ( 3, 4, 9 ) and ' O '$ be the mid-point of $PQwhich is on the $given line 

\dfrac{x - 1}{3} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z - 2}{1} =$\lambda$ (say)

$⇒ x = 3\lambda + 1, y = 2\lambda - 1, z = \lambda + 2$

let \left(3\lambda + 1, 2\lambda - 1, \lambda + 2\right) be$ the co-ordinates ofO$.

Direction ratios of the line is ${a}_{1} = 3, {b}_{1} = 2, {c}_{1} = 1$

Also, direction ratios of $PO$ are

\left(3\lambda - 2, 2\lambda - 5, \lambda - 7\right)

As, $PO$ is perpendicular to the line

$3$\left(3\lambda - 2\right)$ + 2$\left(2\lambda - 5\right)$ + \lambda - 7 = 0$

$⇒ 14\lambda - 23 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = $\dfrac{23}{14}$

$∴ O$ point is $\left(3 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} +1, 2 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} -1, \dfrac{23}{14} +2\right)$

Since, $O$ is mid-point of $PQ$

$∴ \left(3 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} + 1, 2 \cdot \dfrac{23}{14} - 1$, $\dfrac{23}{14} + 2\right)$ = $\left(\dfrac{3 + \alpha}{2}, \dfrac{4 + \beta}{2}, \dfrac{9 + \gamma}{2}\right)$

So, on comparing both side and solving we get,

$\alpha = \dfrac{62}{7}, \beta = \dfrac{4}{7}, \gamma = \dfrac{- 12}{7}$

Hence, $14\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 108$

37977.text: Let $O$ be the origin, and $M$ and $N$ be the points on the lines $\dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 4}{1} = \dfrac{z - 5}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x + 8}{12} = \dfrac{y + 2}{5} = \dfrac{z + 11}{9}$ respectively such that $MN$ is the shortest distance between the given lines. Then $\overset{\to}{OM} \cdot \overset{\to}{ON}$ is equal to _________.
37977.sol:
Let,

${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x - 5}{4} = \dfrac{y - 4}{1} = \dfrac{z - 5}{3} = \lambda$

$⇒ M ( 4\lambda + 5, \lambda + 4, 3\lambda + 5 )$

And ${L}_{2}: \dfrac{x + 8}{12} = \dfrac{y + 2}{5} = \dfrac{z + 11}{9} = \mu$

$⇒ N ( 12\mu - 8, 5\mu - 2, 9\mu - 11 )$

Now, finding $\overset{\to}{MN} = ( 4\lambda - 12\mu + 13, \lambda - 5\mu + 6, 3\lambda - 9\mu + 16 ) . . \ldots \left(1\right)

Now finding cross product$ of direction ratios of line we get,

\overset{\to}{b}1 \times \overset{\to}{b}2 = $\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 4 & 1 & 3 \\ 12 & 5 & 9\end{cases}\right| = - 6\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{k} \ldots . . . \left(2\right)

Now, solving$ the $equation \left(1\right) \text{$ and } $\left(2\right)$ as they are parallel vectors, we get,

$∴ \dfrac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{- 6} = \dfrac{\lambda - 5\mu + 6}{0} = \dfrac{3\lambda - 9\mu + 16}{8}$

Taking $\dfrac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{- 6} = \dfrac{\lambda - 5\mu + 6}{0}

$⇒ \lambda - 5\mu + 6 = 0 \ldots $\left(3\right)$

Taking $\dfrac{4\lambda - 12\mu + 13}{- 6} = \dfrac{3\lambda - 9\mu + 16}{8}

$\lambda - 3\mu + 4 = 0 \ldots $\left(4\right)$

Solve $\left(3\right)$ and $\left(4\right)$ we get

$\lambda = - 1, \mu = 1$

So, $M ( 1, 3, 2 ) and N ( 4, 3, - 2 )$

Hence, $\overset{\to}{OM} \cdot \overset{\to}{ON} = 4 + 9 - 4 = 9$

38416.text: The value of $sin10 ° sin30 ° sin50 ° sin70 °$ is:
38416.sol:
$sin10 ° sin30 ° sin50 ° sin70 °$

$= sin10 ° \times \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 2sin50 ° sin70 °\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}sin10 ° \left(2sin50 ° sin70 °\right)$

Using $2sinAsinB = cos\left(A - B\right) - cos\left(A + B\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}sin10 ° \left(cos20 ° - cos120 °\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}sin10 ° \left(cos20 ° - cos\left(90 ° + 30 °\right)\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}sin10 ° \left(cos20 ° + sin30 °\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{4}sin10 ° \left(cos20 ° + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{8}\left(2sin10 ° cos20 ° + sin10 °\right)$

Again, using $2sinAcosB = sin\left(A + B\right) - sin\left(A - B\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{8}\left(sin30 ° - sin10 ° + sin10 °\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{16} .$

38585.text: Let $\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}, \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{c} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ be the three given vectors. 38585.sol:
Since vector $\overset{\to}{v}, \overset{\to}{a} \text{$ and $} \overset{\to}{b}$ are coplanar then, $\overset{\to}{v} = {\lambda}_{1}\overset{\to}{a} + {\lambda}_{2}\overset{\to}{b}$, where ${\lambda}_{1}, {\lambda}_{2} \in \mathbb{R}$.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = \left({\lambda}_{1} + 2{\lambda}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left({\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(2{\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$∵$ Projection of $\overset{\to}{v}$ on $\overset{\to}{c}$ is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{\lambda}_{1} + 2{\lambda}_{2} - {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} + 2{\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$

$∴ {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} = 1 . . . \left(1\right)$

and $\overset{\to}{v} \cdot \overset{^}{j} = 7 ⇒ {\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2} = 7 . . . \left(2\right)

$⇒ \overset{\to}{v} = $\left({\lambda}_{1} + 2{\lambda}_{2}\right)$\overset{^}{i} + $\left({\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2}\right)$\overset{^}{j} + $\left(2{\lambda}_{1} + {\lambda}_{2}\right)$\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ {\lambda}_{1} + 3{\lambda}_{2} = 1 . . . $\left(1\right)$

$⇒ {\lambda}_{1} - 3{\lambda}_{2} = 7\left(2\right)
From equation \left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right), we get

${\lambda}_{1} = 4, {\lambda}_{2} = - 1$

$∴ \overset{\to}{v} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} + 7\overset{^}{k}$

$∴ \overset{\to}{v} \cdot $\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ = 2 + 7 = 9$

40316.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : EM waves used for optical communication have longer wavelengths than that of microwave, employed in Radar technology.

Reason R : Infrared EM waves are more energetic than microwaves, (used in Radar)

In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
40316.sol:
An optical telecommunication is communication at a distance using light to carry information. It can be performed visually or by using electronic devices.

The wavelength of the microwaves are greater than that of the common optical light waves.

Hence, the Assertion is not correct. But, because of the small wavelength, the electromagnetic waves are more energetic than the microwaves. Hence, the reason is true.

42662.subject: Physics
42662.text: The time period of a simple harmonic oscillator is $T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$. Measured value of mass $(m)$ of the object is 10 g with an accuracy of 10 mg and time for 50 oscillations of the spring is found to be 60 s using a watch of 2 s resolution. Percentage error in determination of spring constant $(k)$ is $\_\_\_\_$ \%.
42662.sol:
The given formula for time period is
$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$.
Squaring both sides, we get $T^2 = 4\pi^2 \frac{k}{m}$, which gives $k = \frac{4\pi^2 m}{T^2}$.
The relative error in $k$ is given by $\frac{\Delta k}{k} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2\frac{\Delta T}{T}$.
Given: $m = 10$ g, $\Delta m = 10$ mg $= 0.01$ g.
Total time for $n=50$ oscillations is $t = 60$ s with resolution $\Delta t = 2$ s.
Since $T = t/n$, the relative error in $T$ is the same as in $t$: $\frac{\Delta T}{T} = \frac{\Delta t}{t}$.
Substituting the values: $\frac{\Delta k}{k} = \frac{0.01}{10} + 2\left(\frac{2}{60}\right)$.
$\frac{\Delta k}{k} = 0.001 + \frac{2}{30} = 0.001 + 0.0666...$
Percentage error $= \left(0.001 + \frac{1}{15}\right) \times 100 = 0.1 + \frac{100}{15} = 0.1 + 6.666... = 6.766...\%$.
Rounding to two decimal places, we get $6.76\%$.

46088.text: A sphere of mass $m$ moving with velocity $v$ hits inelastically with another stationary sphere of same mass. The ratio of their final velocities will be (in terms of $e$ )

As coefficient of restitution, $e=\frac{v_2-v_1}{u_1-u_2}=\frac{v_2-v_1}{u-0} \Rightarrow \quad v_2-v_1=e u$...(i)
By conservation of momentum,
Momentum before collision = Momentum after collision
$\begin{aligned} & m u=m v_1+m v_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad v_1+v_2=u \\ & \end{aligned}$...(ii)
On solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
$\begin{aligned} & v_1=\frac{u}{2}(1-e) \text{ and } v_2=\frac{u}{2}(1+e) \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{v_1}{v_2}=\frac{1-e}{1+e} \\ & \end{aligned}$

46375.sol:
The velocity with which water will came out
$v=\sqrt{2 g(H-h)}$
The time of flight of water ejected from the hole.
$\begin{aligned} t & =\sqrt{\frac{2 h}{g}}=\text{ time of flight } \\ \therefore \quad x & =v \times t \\ & =\sqrt{2 g(H-h)} \times \sqrt{\frac{2 h}{g}}=\sqrt{4\left(H h-h^2\right)}\end{aligned}$
For $x$ to be maximum
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d x}{d h}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & d \frac{\sqrt{4\left(H h-h^2\right)}}{d h}=0 \\ \Rightarrow & 0=H-2 h \Rightarrow h=\frac{H}{2}\end{aligned}$

46717.subject: Physics
46717.text: A tuning fork $A$ produces 4 beats/s with another tuning fork $B$ of frequency 320 Hz . On filing one of the prongs of $A, 4$ beats $/ \mathrm{s}$ are again heard when sounded with the same fork $B$. Then, the frequency of the fork $A$ before filing is
46717.sol:
There are 4 beats between $A$ and $B$, therefore the possible frequencies of $A$ are 316 or 324 that is $(320 \pm 4) \mathrm{Hz}$.
When the prong of $A$ is filed, its frequency becomes greater than the original frequency. If we assume that original frequency of $A$ is 324 then on filing its frequency will be greater than 324 . The beats between $A$ and $B$ will be more than 4 . But it is given that the beats are again 4 , therefore, 324 is not possible.
Therefore, required frequency must be 316 Hz . (This is true, because on filing the frequency may increase so as to give 4 beats with $B$ of frequency 320 Hz).

47306.subject: Chemistry
47306.text: Glycerol is a trihydric alcohol. It contains ____.
options: One primary, one secondary and one tertiary alcoholic groups
Two primary and one secondary alcoholic groups
Two secondary and one primary alcoholic groups
One primary and two tertiary alcoholic groups
47306.sol:
The chemical formula of glycerol is $CH_2(OH)-CH(OH)-CH_2(OH)$.

The two terminal $-OH$ groups are attached to primary carbon atoms ($-CH_2-$), making them primary alcoholic groups.

The middle $-OH$ group is attached to a secondary carbon atom ($-CH-$), making it a secondary alcoholic group.

Therefore, glycerol contains two primary and one secondary alcoholic groups.

Answer: Two primary and one secondary alcoholic groups

56452.subject: Chemistry
56452.text: What is EAN of metal ion in hexacyanoferrate (II) ion?
56452.sol:
The Effective Atomic Number (EAN) for the metal ion in $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$ is determined through systematic analysis of its electronic configuration.

The central metal ion is iron with atomic number $Z = 26$. The oxidation state calculation yields $x + 6 \times (-1) = -4$, resulting in $x = +2$ for $\text{Fe}^{2+}$.

The number of electrons in $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $26 - 2 = 24$. Each cyanide ligand donates 2 electrons, with 6 ligands contributing $6 \times 2 = 12$ electrons.

EAN $= 24 + 12 = 36$

Therefore, the Effective Atomic Number is $\boxed{36}$.

57583.subject: Chemistry
57583.text: What is the importance of Sandmeyer's reaction?
options: To obtain Ar-X by replacing diazo group of $\text{AR-N}_2^+\text{-X}^-$ using $\text{CuCl}$ / $\text{HCl}$
To obtain R-F from R-Cl using AgF
To obtain $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-R}$ from R-CO-R using Zn-Hg / HCl
57583.sol:
Sandmeyer's reaction is a chemical reaction used to synthesize aryl halides from aryl diazonium salts. It involves the replacement of the diazonium group ($-\text{N}_2^+$) in $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{X}^-$ by a halogen atom (such as Cl or Br) or a cyanide group using copper(I) salts like $\text{CuCl}/\text{HCl}$, $\text{CuBr}/\text{HBr}$, or $\text{CuCN}/\text{KCN}$.

The reaction to obtain R-I from R-Cl is known as the Finkelstein reaction.

The reaction to obtain R-F from R-Cl using AgF is known as the Swarts reaction.

The reaction to obtain $\text{R-CH}_2\text{-R}$ from R-CO-R using Zn-Hg / HCl is known as the Clemmensen reduction.

Therefore, Sandmeyer's reaction is used to obtain Ar-X by replacing the diazo group of $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{X}^-$ using $\text{CuCl}$ / $\text{HCl}$.

Answer: To obtain Ar-X by replacing diazo group of $\text{AR-N}_2^+\text{-X}^-$ using $\text{CuCl}$ / $\text{HCl}$

57593.subject: Chemistry
57593.text: What is the order of reactivity of alkyl halides with ammonia?
57593.sol:
Reactivity of alkyl halides with ammonia depends on nucleophilic substitution mechanisms, where ammonia acts as a nucleophile. The key factor is the leaving group ability of the halide ion.

Leaving group ability is inversely related to basicity. Comparing halides: iodine is the weakest base and thus the best leaving group, followed by bromine and then chlorine. This gives the order I^{-} > Br^{-} > Cl^{-} for leaving group quality.

Consequently, alkyl halide reactivity follows: $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl}$.

Evaluating the options:
A) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I}$ (Incorrect)
B) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl}$ (Incorrect)
C) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl}$ (Correct)
D) $\mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{Cl} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{I} > \mathrm{R}{-}\mathrm{B}$ (Incorrect)

Answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

58241.subject: Chemistry
58241.text: Which of the following inert gases is used for magnetic resonance imaging?
58241.sol:
The correct answer is A) He.

Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machines utilize powerful superconducting magnets that require cooling to approximately 4 Kelvin to maintain their superconducting state. Liquid helium serves as the optimal cryogenic coolant due to its exceptionally low boiling point of 4.2 K at atmospheric pressure, which is capable of achieving these ultra-low temperatures. Its inert nature prevents chemical reactions with MRI components.

Other inert gases—neon, argon, and xenon—have significantly higher boiling points and cannot reach the necessary temperature range for superconducting magnet operation.

59668.subject: Chemistry
59668.text: Which parameter is indicated by the number of waves passing through a given point in one second?
59668.sol:
Frequency refers to the number of waves passing through a given point in one second. It is typically measured in Hertz $(\mathrm{Hz})$, where 1 Hz is equal to one wave passing per second.
Here's a brief explanation of the other options:
- (A) Wavelength: The distance between two consecutive points in phase on a wave (e.g., from crest to crest or trough to trough).
- (C) Wave number: The number of wavelengths per unit distance, typically measured in inverse meters ( $1 / \mathrm{m}$ ).
- (D) Amplitude: The maximum displacement of a wave from its equilibrium position, related to the wave's intensity but not its frequency.

59784.text: Which from following gases is adsorbed to greater extent if adsorbent remains same at similar conditions of temperature and pressure?
59784.sol:
The extent of adsorption in physisorption depends on the ease of gas liquefaction, which correlates directly with critical temperature $T_c$.

The critical temperatures are: $\mathrm{H}_2$ at 33 K, $\mathrm{N}_2$ at 126 K, $\mathrm{O}_2$ at 155 K, and $\mathrm{SO}_2$ at 430.65 K.

Increasing order of $T_c$ is $\mathrm{H}_2 < \mathrm{N}_2 < \mathrm{O}_2 < \mathrm{SO}_2$.

$\mathrm{SO}_2$ has the highest critical temperature and will thus be adsorbed most extensively.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

61048.sol:
Evaluate the definite integral: $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} (2+3x^2)\cos 3x\,dx$

Apply integration by parts with $u = 2+3x^2$ and $dv = \cos 3x\,dx$, yielding $du = 6x\,dx$ and $v = \frac{1}{3}\sin 3x$:

$I = \frac{1}{3}(2+3x^2)\sin 3x - 2\int x\sin 3x\,dx$

Apply integration by parts again to the remaining integral with $u = x$ and $dv = \sin 3x\,dx$, giving $du = dx$ and $v = -\frac{1}{3}\cos 3x$:

$\int x\sin 3x\,dx = -\frac{1}{3}x\cos 3x + \frac{1}{9}\sin 3x$

Substitute back into the expression for $I$:

$I = \frac{1}{3}(2+3x^2)\sin 3x + \frac{2}{3}x\cos 3x - \frac{2}{9}\sin 3x$

Evaluate the definite integral from $0$ to $\frac{\pi}{6}$:

At $x = \frac{\pi}{6}$:
$\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1$, $\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0$
$\frac{1}{3}(2+3(\frac{\pi}{6})^2)(1) + \frac{2}{3}(\frac{\pi}{6})(0) - \frac{2}{9}(1) = \frac{4}{9} + \frac{\pi^2}{36}$

At $x = 0$, the expression evaluates to $0$.

Final result: $\frac{4}{9} + \frac{\pi^2}{36}$

61339.text: If $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{y}(x)$ and $\left(\frac{2+\sin x}{\mathrm{y}+1}\right) \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{d} x}=-\cos x$, $y(0)=1$, then $y\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=$
61339.sol:
Solution

The differential equation is solved by separating variables:

$\frac{dy}{y+1} = -\frac{\cos x}{2+\sin x} dx$

Integrating both sides:

$\int \frac{1}{y+1} dy = \int -\frac{\cos x}{2+\sin x} dx$

The left integral is $\ln |y+1|$.
For the right, substitute $u = 2+\sin x$, $du = \cos x dx$, yielding $-\ln |2+\sin x|$.

Combining constants of integration:

$\ln |y+1| + \ln |2+\sin x| = C$

Exponentiating gives $(y+1)(2+\sin x) = K$, with $K$ constant.

Applying $y(0)=1$: $(1+1)(2+0) = 4 = K$.

Thus, $(y+1)(2+\sin x) = 4$.

Evaluating at $x = \frac{\pi}{2}$, where $\sin \frac{\pi}{2} = 1$:

$(y(\frac{\pi}{2})+1)(2+1) = 4$

$(y(\frac{\pi}{2})+1) = \frac{4}{3}$

$y(\frac{\pi}{2}) = \frac{1}{3}$.

The answer is $\boxed{A}$.

61661.sol:
Let $y = \log_8(\log_5 x)$

Using the change of base formula, we can write:

$y = \dfrac{\log_e(\log_5 x)}{\log_e 8}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\log_e 8} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\log_5 x} \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log_5 x)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\log_e 8} \cdot \dfrac{1}{\log_5 x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x \log_e 5}$

Substitute $\log_5 x = \dfrac{\log_e x}{\log_e 5}$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{\log_e 8} \cdot \dfrac{\log_e 5}{\log_e x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x \log_e 5}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{x \log_e 8 \log_e x}$

Assuming $\log$ represents the natural logarithm $\log_e$, we get:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{x \log 8 \log x}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{x\log 8\log x}$

The word INSTITUTION has $11$ letters.

I appears $3$ times.

63642.subject: Mathematics
63642.text: In a single toss of a fair die, the odds against the event that number 4 or 5 turns up is
63642.sol:
The sample space for a fair die toss is $S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}$ with $n(S) = 6$ total outcomes.

Let $E$ represent the event that a 4 or 5 appears, so $E = \{4, 5\}$ with $n(E) = 2$ favorable outcomes.
The probability is $P(E) = \frac{n(E)}{n(S)} = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$.

The odds against $E$ are expressed as $P(E') : P(E)$, where $E'$ denotes the complement of $E$.
The complement consists of outcomes $\{1, 2, 3, 6\}$, so $P(E') = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$.

The odds ratio becomes $\frac{2}{3} : \frac{1}{3}$, which simplifies to $2 : 1$ after multiplying both terms by 3.

Odds against the event: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

70150.text: The ratio of intensities at two points on the screen in Young's double slit experiment when waves from the two slits have a path difference of zero and $\lambda/4$ is (\lambda$ is the wavelength of light used) (\cos 0^{}^{\circ} = 1$, $\cos\pi/2 = 0$)
70150.sol:
The phase difference $\phi$ is related to the path difference $\Delta x$ by the relation $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$.

The intensity at any point on the screen is given by $I = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right), where $I_0is the $maximum intensity.

For the first point, the path difference is \Delta$ x_1 = 0$.

$\phi_1 = 0 \Rightarrow I_1 = I_0 \cos^2(0) = I_0

For the $second point, the path difference is \Delta$ x_2 = $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}.

$\phi_2 = $\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \dfrac{\lambda}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}

$ I_2 = I_0 \cos^2$\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) =$ I_0 $\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}

The ratio$ of $intensities is \dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{I_0}{I_0/2} = \dfrac{2}{1}.

Answer: 2 : 1$

70437.subject: Physics
70437.text: When a sonometer wire vibrates in the third overtone, the number of antinodes and nodes formed on the wire are respectively
70437.sol:
A sonometer wire is fixed at both ends.

For a string fixed at both ends, the $n$-th overtone corresponds to the $(n+1)$-th harmonic, which consists of $n+1$ loops.

For the third overtone, $n = 3$.

Number of loops $= 3 + 1 = 4$.

Since each loop contains exactly one antinode, the number of antinodes is $4$.

The number of nodes on a string fixed at both ends is always one more than the number of antinodes.

Number of nodes $= 4 + 1 = 5$.

Thus, the number of antinodes and nodes are $4$ and $5$ respectively.

Answer: $4, 5$

71030.subject: Biology
71030.text: Some amount of carbon dissolved into oceanic water remains as sediments of carbon in the sea in the form of __________ and is removed from circulation.
71030.sol:
Carbon dioxide dissolved in oceanic water reacts with water to form carbonic acid, which dissociates into bicarbonate and carbonate ions. These carbonate ions react with calcium and magnesium ions present in seawater to form insoluble calcium carbonate and magnesium carbonate.

These insoluble carbonates precipitate and settle at the bottom of the ocean, forming sedimentary rocks such as limestone and dolomite. This process effectively removes carbon from the active carbon cycle and stores it as sediments.

Carbonates of sodium and potassium are highly soluble in water and do not form sediments. Carbonic acid remains dissolved in water.

Answer: carbonates of Ca and Mg

71095.subject: Biology
71095.text: Following is a list of evidence to support Darwinism, EXCEPT____________.
options: evolution of present day long necked Giraffe
existence of neutral flowers and sterility of hybrids
evolution of black coloured moth as new species
71095.sol:
Darwinism is supported by many evidences such as the evolution of the long-necked giraffe through survival of the fittest, the development of DDT resistance in mosquitoes, and industrial melanism (evolution of black-coloured moths).

However, the existence of neutral flowers and the sterility of hybrids are considered classic objections to Darwinism. Natural selection operates on traits that enhance reproductive success, so the development of sterile hybrids and neutral (sterile) flowers cannot be easily explained by Darwin's original theory.

Answer: existence of neutral flowers and sterility of hybrids

71832.subject: Chemistry
71832.text: Which of the following is not an allylic halide?
71832.sol:
An allylic halide is a compound in which the halogen atom is bonded to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom that is adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond.

Let us examine the structure of each option:

4-bromopent-2-ene: $CH_3-CH=CH-CH(Br)-CH_3$
The bromine atom is attached to C4, which is an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to the C2=C3 double bond. It is an allylic halide.

3-bromo-2-methylbut-1-ene: $CH_2=C(CH_3)-CH(Br)-CH_3$
The bromine atom is attached to C3, which is an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to the C1=C2 double bond. It is an allylic halide.

1-bromobut-2-ene: $Br-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_3$
The bromine atom is attached to C1, which is an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to the C2=C3 double bond. It is an allylic halide.

4-bromobut-1-ene: $CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH_2-Br$
The bromine atom is attached to C4, which is an $sp^3$ carbon adjacent to C3 (another $sp^3$ carbon), not the double bond. Thus, it is not an allylic halide.

Answer: 4-bromobut-1-ene

77497.text: What is $\int \frac{x^4-1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}} d x$ equal to?
77497.sol:
Take option (1)
$I_1=\sqrt{\frac{x^4+x^3+1}{x}}+C\begin{aligned}

\frac{d I_2}{d x} & =\frac{1}{2}\left(x^3+x^2+x^{-1}\right)^{-1 / 2}\left(3 x^2+2 x-x^{-2}\right) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{3 x^2+2 x-\frac{1}{x^2}}{\sqrt{x^3+x^2+\frac{1}{x}}}\right] \\

\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}

& =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{4 x^3+\frac{2}{x^3}}{\sqrt{x^4+2-\frac{1}{x^2}}}\right]=\frac{2 x^6+1}{\frac{x^3}{x} \sqrt{x^6+2 x^2-1}} \\

77850.subject: Mathematics
77850.text: In how many ways can the letters of the word DELHI be arranged keeping the positions of vowels and consonants unchanged?
77850.sol:
The word DELHI consists of $5$ letters: $3$ consonants (D, L, H) and $2$ vowels (E, I).

The arrangement of letters in the word is Consonant-Vowel-Consonant-Consonant-Vowel.

Since the positions of vowels and consonants must remain unchanged, the consonants can only be placed in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th positions, and the vowels can only be placed in the $2$nd and $5$th positions.

The $3$ consonants can be arranged in their $3$ positions in $3!$ ways.

The $2$ vowels can be arranged in their $2$ positions in $2!$ ways.

Total number of arrangements = $3! \times 2! = 6 \times 2 = 12$.

Answer: $12$

78188.text:
If a, b and $c(a \gt 0, c \gt 0)$ are in GP, then consider the following in respect of the equation $a x^2+b x+c=0:$
1. The equation has imaginary roots.
2. The ratio of the roots of the equation is $1: \omega$ where $\omega$ is a cube root of unity.
3. The product of roots of the equation is $\left(\frac{b^2}{a^2}\right)$.

78188.sol:
Given that $a, b, c$ are in GP
$\therefore \quad b^2=a c$
Now, $a x^2+b x+c=0\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{D} & =b^2-4 a c \\
& =a c-4 a c=-3 a c \lt 0
\end{aligned}$
1. $\therefore$ Roots are imaginary (correct)
Let, $\quad a=2, b=4, c=8\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad x^2+2 x+4 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x & =\frac{-2 \pm \sqrt{4-16}}{2}=-1 \pm \sqrt{3}
\end{aligned}$
2. Ratio of roots $=\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}}{-1-\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\omega}{\omega^2}=\frac{1}{\omega}$ (correct)
3.$\begin{aligned}
\text{ Product of roots } & =\frac{(-1+\sqrt{3})(-1-\sqrt{3})}{2} \times 4 \\
& =\omega \cdot \omega^2 \cdot 4=4=\frac{b^2}{a^2}
\end{aligned}$ (correct)
Hence, statements 1,2 and 3 are correct.

78823.subject: Mathematics
78823.text: A sphere of constant radius $r$ through the origin intersects the coordinate axes in $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and C. What is the locus of the centroid of the triangle ABC ?
78823.sol:
Let the sphere passing through points $A(a, 0,0)$, $\mathrm{B}(0, \mathrm{ b}, 0), \mathrm{C}(0,0, \mathrm{c})$
Equation of sphere is $x^2+y^2+z^2-a x-b y-c z=0$ radius, $\mathrm{r}=\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2+\mathrm{c}^2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2+\mathrm{c}^2=4 \mathrm{r}^2....(1)$
(Squaring on both sides)
Let $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ be centroid of sphere.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)=\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}+0+0}{3}, \frac{0+\mathrm{b}+0}{3}, \frac{0+0+\mathrm{c}}{3}\right) \\
& =\left(\frac{\mathrm{a}}{3}, \frac{\mathrm{ b}}{3}, \frac{\mathrm{c}}{3}\right) \\
& \therefore \alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=\frac{\mathrm{a}^2}{9}+\frac{\mathrm{b}^2}{9}+\frac{\mathrm{c}^2}{9} \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{a}^2+\mathrm{b}^2+\mathrm{c}^2}{9} \\
& =\frac{4 \mathrm{r}^2}{9}....from(1) \\
& \Rightarrow 9\left(\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2\right)=4 \mathrm{r}^2
\end{aligned}$
So, Locus is $9\left(x^2+y^2+z^2\right)=4 r^2$.

options: is membrane-bound and contains storage proteins and lipids
is membrane-bound and contains water and excretory substances
lacks membrane and contains water and excretory substances
79786.sol: The cytoplasm of many plant and some animal cells contains numerous small or large sized, hollow, liquid filled structures, the vacuoles. The vacuoles of plant cells are bounded by a single semipermeable membrane known as tonoplast. These vacuoles contain water, phenol, flavonols, anthocyanins, alkaloids and storage products such as sugars and proteins. The vacuoles of animal cells are bounded by a lipoproteinaceous membrane and their function is storage, transmission of materials and maintenance of internal pressure of cell.

79896.subject: Botany
79896.text:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. ProductivityI. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses
B. Net primary productivityII. Rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
C. Gross primary productivityIII. Rate of biomass production
D. Secondary productivityIV. Rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
79896.sol:
Productivity is defined as the rate of biomass production.

Gross primary productivity (GPP) of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.

Net primary productivity (NPP) is the gross primary productivity minus respiration losses ($R$), which is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs.

Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

85383.subject: Zoology
85383.text: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is not completely curable?
85383.sol: Herpes simplex type 1 or 2 viruses causes genital herpes, an infection of the skin and mucous membranes in the genital and surrounding areas. Herpes simplex virus usually spreads, when in contact with blisters. However, people with genital herpes can shed the virus from the genital area and infect others even without a blister being present. Cold sores on the mouth are a potential source of genital infection during mouth-to-genital contact. Medications can help decrease the severity of the herpes lesions and prevent recurrences, but they do not cure the infection.

86105.subject: Chemistry
86105.text: The compound that produces aromatic species upon deprotonation of the indicated hydrogen is:
86105.sol:
For a species to be aromatic, it must be cyclic, planar, completely conjugated, and contain $(4n+2)$ $\pi$ electrons (Huckel's rule).

Deprotonation involves the removal of $H^{+}$ to form a carbanion.

In compound (1), deprotonation forms a carbanion that can delocalize to form an enolate, but the ring contains an $sp^{3}$ hybridized carbon, so it lacks complete conjugation. It is non-aromatic.

In compound (2), deprotonation yields the 5-methylcyclopentadienyl anion. The ring is cyclic, planar, completely conjugated, and possesses $6$ $\pi$ electrons ($4$ from two double bonds and $2$ from the carbanion lone pair). This satisfies the $(4n+2)$ $\pi$ rule for $n=1$, making the species aromatic.

In compound (3), deprotonation gives the 3-methylcyclopropenyl anion. The ring is fully conjugated but has $4$ $\pi$ electrons. It satisfies the $4n$ $\pi$ rule for $n=1$, making it antiaromatic.

In compound (4), deprotonation forms the 7-methylcycloheptatrienyl anion. The conjugated ring has $8$ $\pi$ electrons. It satisfies the $4n$ $\pi$ rule for $n=2$, making it antiaromatic.

Therefore, compound (2) produces an aromatic species upon deprotonation.

Answer :

Hence, the required probability $= \mathop{\mathop{\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2}}_{⏟}}_{\left(HTTHH\right)} + \mathop{\mathop{\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2}}_{⏟}}_{\left(THTHH\right)} + \mathop{\mathop{\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2}}_{⏟}}_{\left(TTTHH\right)}$
$= \dfrac{3}{32}$

$= m^{2} + 2mn + n^{2} - m^{2}$
$⇒ 4{5}^{2} - 2{1}^{2} = ${\left(m + n\right)}^{2} - m^{2}$
$⇒ m + n = 45 and m = 21$
$⇒ n = 24 and m = 21$
Hence, the numbers are

92496.text: Monochromatic radiation of wavelength $\text{\lambda}$ is incident on a hydrogen sample in ground state. Hydrogen atoms absorb a fraction of light and subsequently emit radiation of six different wavelengths. Find the value of $\text{\lambda}$.
92496.sol:
As the hydrogen atoms emit radiation of six different wavelengths, some of them must have been excited to $\text{n} = 4$, The energy in $\text{n} = 4$ state is

${E}_{4} = \dfrac{{E}_{1}}{{4}^{2}} = - \dfrac{1 3 \cdot 6 \text{e} \text{V}}{1 6} = - 0 \cdot 8 5 \text{eV.}$

The energy needed to take a hydrogen atom from its ground state to $\text{n} = 4$ is

$\text{13}\text{.6 eV - 0}\text{.85 eV = 12}\text{.75 eV}$ .

The photons of the incident radiation should have $12.75\text{eV}$ of energy. So

$\dfrac{\text{hc}}{\lambda} = 1 2 \cdot 7 5 \text{eV}$

or , $\lambda = \dfrac{\text{hc}}{1 2 \cdot 7 5 \text{eV}}$

$= \dfrac{1 2 4 2 \text{eV} \text{nm}}{1 2 \cdot 7 5 \text{eV}}$

$\text{= 97}\text{.5 nm}$.

94555.text: A uniform copper rod of $50cm$ length is insulated on the sides and has its ends exposed to ice and steam respectively. If there is a layer of water $1mm$ thick at each end, the temperature gradient $\left(in ° C{m}^{- 1}\right)$ in the bar is (assume that the thermal conductivity of copper is $400W{m}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$ and water is $0 .4 W{m}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$ )
94555.sol:
Given, ${K}_{c} = 400W{m}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1},$

${K}_{w} = 0.4W{m}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$

${\theta}_{1} = 100 ° C, {\theta}_{2} = 0 ° C$



In steady-state, the flow of heat will be the same throughout the whole system

$\dfrac{{K}_{w}A\left(100 - \theta\right)}{{10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{{K}_{c}A\left(\theta - \theta′\right)}{\left(\dfrac{50}{100}\right)}$

Or $\left(100 - \theta\right) = \dfrac{{K}_{c}}{{K}_{w}} \times {10}^{- 3} \times \dfrac{\left(\theta - {\theta}^{′}\right)}{0.5}$

$= \dfrac{400}{0.4} \times {10}^{- 3} \times \dfrac{\left(\theta - \theta′\right)}{0.5}$

$\left(100 - \theta\right) = 2\left(\theta - \theta′\right)$

$\dfrac{( 100 - \theta ) {K}_{w} A}{{10}^{- 3}} = \dfrac{( {\theta}^{′} - 0 ) {K}_{w} A}{{10}^{- 3}}$

$100 - \theta = {\theta}^{′}$

Or $\left(100 - \theta\right) = 4\theta - 200$

$⇒ 5\theta = 300 ⇒ \theta = 60 ° C$

$∴ {\theta}^{′} = 100 - \theta = 100 - 60 = 40 ° C$

Hence, the temperature gradient along the bar

$= \dfrac{\theta - \theta′}{0.5} = \dfrac{60 - 40}{0.5} = 40 ° C{m}^{- 1}$

100109.subject: Physics
100109.text: A physical quantity $X$ is related to the permittivity of free space $\varepsilon_0$, Planck's constant $h$, and the speed of light $c$ by the relation $X \propto \varepsilon_0^\alpha h^\beta c^\gamma$. If the values of the exponents are $\alpha = -1/2$, $\beta = 1/2$, and $\gamma = 1/2$, then the quantity $X$ represents:
100109.sol:
First, write the dimensional formulas for the given fundamental constants:
Permittivity of free space $[\varepsilon_0] = [M^{-1} L^{-3} T^4 A^2]$
Planck's constant $[h] = [M L^2 T^{-1}]$
Speed of light $[c] = [L T^{-1}]$

Substitute the given exponents into the relation $X \propto \varepsilon_0^{-1/2} h^{1/2} c^{1/2}$:
$[X] = [M^{-1} L^{-3} T^4 A^2]^{-1/2} [M L^2 T^{-1}]^{1/2} [L T^{-1}]^{1/2}$

Simplify the powers for each dimension:
For $M$: $(-1)(-1/2) + (1)(1/2) + (0) = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1$
For $L$: $(-3)(-1/2) + (2)(1/2) + (1)(1/2) = 3/2 + 1 + 1/2 = 3$
For $T$: $(4)(-1/2) + (-1)(1/2) + (-1)(1/2) = -2 - 1/2 - 1/2 = -3$
For $A$: $(2)(-1/2) = -1$

The dimensional formula for $X$ is $[M L^3 T^{-3} A^{-1}]$.

Now, check the dimensions of the given options:
Electric field $E = \dfrac{F}{q} = \dfrac{[M L T^{-2}]}{[A T]} = [M L T^{-3} A^{-1}]$
Electric flux $\Phi_E = E \times \text{Area} = [M L T^{-3} A^{-1}] \times [L^2] = [M L^3 T^{-3} A^{-1}]$
Electric potential $V = \dfrac{W}{q} = \dfrac{[M L^2 T^{-2}]}{[A T]} = [M L^2 T^{-3} A^{-1}]$
Magnetic flux $\Phi_B = [M L^2 T^{-2} A^{-1}]$

Therefore, $X$ represents electric flux.

Answer: Electric flux

100699.subject: Physics
100699.text: A block is sliding down a rough inclined plane of inclination $30^{\circ}$ with a constant acceleration of $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$. If $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is:
100699.sol:
The equation of motion for a block sliding down a rough inclined plane is given by:

$mg \sin \theta - f_k = ma$

where $f_k = \mu_k N = \mu_k mg \cos \theta$.

Substituting the expression for kinetic friction:

$mg \sin \theta - \mu_k mg \cos \theta = ma$

Dividing the entire equation by $m$:

$g \sin \theta - \mu_k g \cos \theta = a$

Substitute the given values ($g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\theta = 30^{\circ}$, $a = 2.5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$):

$10 \sin 30^{\circ} - \mu_k (10) \cos 30^{\circ} = 2.5$

$10 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) - \mu_k (10) \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 2.5$

$5 - 5\sqrt{3} \mu_k = 2.5$

$5\sqrt{3} \mu_k = 5 - 2.5 = 2.5$

$\mu_k = \dfrac{2.5}{5\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$

102408.text: A particle executing simple harmonic motion has a time period of $4 \text{ s}$ and an amplitude of $6 \text{ m}$. If it starts its motion from the positive extreme position at $t = 0$, the equation of its displacement $x$ as a function of time $t$ is
102408.sol:
Given, time period $T = 4 \text{ s}$ and amplitude $A = 6 \text{ m}$.

The angular frequency $\omega$ is given by:
$\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} \text{ rad/s}$

The general equation for the displacement of a particle in SHM is:
$x = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$

Since the particle starts from the positive extreme position at $t = 0$, its initial phase $\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Substituting the values into the general equation:
$x = 6 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin\left(\theta + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \cos(\theta)$, we get:
$x = 6 \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{2}\right)$

Answer: $x = 6 \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{2}\right)$

102415.subject: Physics
102415.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The motion of a particle described by the position vector $\vec{r} = A \cos(\omega t) \hat{i} + B \sin(\omega t) \hat{j}$ (where $A \neq B$) is an elliptical trajectory, and the net force acting on the particle is always directed towards one of the foci of the ellipse.

Reason (R): The acceleration of the particle satisfies the relation $\vec{a} = -\omega^2 \vec{r}$, representing a central restoring force directed towards the origin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
102415.sol:
For the given position vector $\vec{r} = A \cos(\omega t) \hat{i} + B \sin(\omega t) \hat{j}$, the coordinates are $x = A \cos(\omega t)$ and $y = B \sin(\omega t)$.

Eliminating $t$, we get $\dfrac{x^2}{A^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{B^2} = 1$, which is the equation of an ellipse. Thus, the trajectory is elliptical.

The acceleration is given by $\vec{a} = \dfrac{d^2\vec{r}}{dt^2} = -\omega^2 [A \cos(\omega t) \hat{i} + B \sin(\omega t) \hat{j}] = -\omega^2 \vec{r}$.

According to Newton's second law, the net force is $\vec{F} = m\vec{a} = -m\omega^2 \vec{r}$. The negative sign indicates that the force is always directed opposite to the position vector, i.e., towards the origin (the center of the ellipse), not towards the foci. Hence, Assertion (A) is false.

The relation $\vec{a} = -\omega^2 \vec{r}$ correctly represents a central restoring force directed towards the origin. Hence, Reason (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true.

102458.text: The variation of kinetic energy with displacement for a spring-mass system executing simple harmonic motion is given by an inverted parabola. The maximum kinetic energy is $16$ J, and the kinetic energy becomes zero at displacements of $+4$ m and $-4$ m from the mean position. The spring constant of the system is :
102458.sol:
The graph of kinetic energy versus displacement is an inverted parabola. The maximum kinetic energy occurs at the mean position (displacement $x = 0$) and represents the total mechanical energy $E$ of the system.

Given maximum kinetic energy, $E = 16$ J.

The kinetic energy becomes zero at the extreme positions, which gives the amplitude $A$ of the oscillation. Thus, $A = 4$ m.

The total energy of a spring-mass system is given by:
$E = \dfrac{1}{2} k A^2$

Substituting the given values:
$16 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times k \times (4)^2$

$16 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times k \times 16$

$k = 2$ N/m.

Answer: $2$ N/m

102548.sol:
Since, the observer is stationary, so when train is approaching towards the observer or moving towards the observer, apparent frequency is given as,
$n^{\prime}=n\left(\frac{v}{v-v_{s}}\right)$
where, $v_{s}$ is the speed of sound.
It is clear from the above expression that $n^{\prime}>n$. However, when the train is going away from the observer, then apparent frequency,
$\begin{array}{ll} 
& n^{\prime}=n\left(\frac{v}{v+v_{s}}\right) \\
\therefore \quad & n^{\prime} < n
\end{array}$
Hence, graph represented in option (d) is correct.

104500.subject: Physics
104500.text: Light enters the flat circular end of an optical fiber at an angle of incidence of $60^{\circ}$. The ray then hits the curved side wall exactly at the critical angle, resulting in grazing emergence into the surrounding air cladding. The refractive index of the fiber core is:
104500.sol:
Let the refractive index of the fiber core be $\mu$ and the angle of refraction at the flat end be $r$.

Applying Snell's law at the flat entry surface:
$1 \times \sin 60^{\circ} = \mu \sin r$
$\sin r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\mu}$

Inside the fiber, the ray strikes the curved side wall. From the geometry of the cylinder, the normal to the side wall is perpendicular to the normal at the flat end. Thus, the angle of incidence at the side wall is $90^{\circ} - r$.

For grazing emergence into the air cladding, this angle must equal the critical angle $c$.
$\sin(90^{\circ} - r) = \sin c = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$
$\cos r = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$

Using the trigonometric identity $\sin^2 r + \cos^2 r = 1$:
$\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2\mu}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)^2 = 1$
$\dfrac{3}{4\mu^2} + \dfrac{1}{\mu^2} = 1$
$\dfrac{7}{4\mu^2} = 1 \Rightarrow \mu^2 = \dfrac{7}{4}$

$\mu = \dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$

104851.subject: Physics
104851.text: What is the ratio of the ionization energy of a hydrogen atom from its first excited state to the ionization energy of a $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ ion from its second excited state?
104851.sol:
The ionization energy from the $n^{\text{th}}$ state of a hydrogen-like species is given by $IE = 13.6 \times \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2} \mathrm{eV}$.

For a hydrogen atom ($Z=1$) in its first excited state ($n=2$):
$IE_1 = 13.6 \times \dfrac{1^2}{2^2} = \dfrac{13.6}{4} \mathrm{eV}$.

For a $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ ion ($Z=2$) in its second excited state ($n=3$):
$IE_2 = 13.6 \times \dfrac{2^2}{3^2} = 13.6 \times \dfrac{4}{9} \mathrm{eV}$.

The ratio of their ionization energies is:
$\dfrac{IE_1}{IE_2} = \dfrac{1/4}{4/9} = \dfrac{9}{16}$.

Thus, the required ratio is $9:16$.

Answer: $9:16$

Given the standard electrode potentials at $298$ K:
$E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}) = +0.34$ V
$E^\circ(\text{Cu}^+/\text{Cu}) = +0.52$ V

The standard electrode potential ($E^\circ$) for the half-cell reaction $\text{Cu}^{2+} + e^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}^+$ is:
114355.sol:
The given half-cell reactions are:

$\text{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}$, $E^\circ_1 = +0.34$ V
$\Delta G^\circ_1 = -n_1FE^\circ_1 = -2 \times F \times (0.34) = -0.68F$

$\text{Cu}^+ + e^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}$, $E^\circ_2 = +0.52$ V
$\Delta G^\circ_2 = -n_2FE^\circ_2 = -1 \times F \times (0.52) = -0.52F$

The required half-cell reaction is:
$\text{Cu}^{2+} + e^- \rightarrow \text{Cu}^+$

This reaction is obtained by subtracting the second reaction from the first reaction:
$\Delta G^\circ_3 = \Delta G^\circ_1 - \Delta G^\circ_2$

$-1 \times F \times E^\circ_3 = -0.68F - (-0.52F)$

$-FE^\circ_3 = -0.16F$

$E^\circ_3 = +0.16$ V

Answer: $+0.16$ V

According to Faraday's Second Law of Electrolysis, when the same quantity of electricity is passed through different electrolytes connected in series, the masses of the substances deposited are proportional to their respective equivalent weights.

$\dfrac{w_{\mathrm{Ag}}}{w_{\mathrm{Cu}}} = \dfrac{E_{\mathrm{Ag}}}{E_{\mathrm{Cu}}}$

The equivalent weight of a metal is its molar mass divided by its valency (n-factor).
For $\mathrm{Ag}$ in $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$, valency $= 1$
$E_{\mathrm{Ag}} = \dfrac{108}{1} = 108$

For $\mathrm{Cu}$ in $\mathrm{CuSO}_4$, valency $= 2$
$E_{\mathrm{Cu}} = \dfrac{63.5}{2} = 31.75$

Substituting the values into the ratio:
$\dfrac{w_{\mathrm{Ag}}}{1.27} = \dfrac{108}{31.75}$

$w_{\mathrm{Ag}} = 1.27 \times \dfrac{108}{31.75} = 1.27 \times 3.4015...$

Alternatively, calculate the number of equivalents of Cu deposited:
Equivalents of $\mathrm{Cu} = \dfrac{1.27}{31.75} = 0.04$

Equivalents of $\mathrm{Ag}$ deposited $= 0.04$
Mass of $\mathrm{Ag} = 0.04 \times 108 = 4.32 \mathrm{~g}$

Answer: $4.32 \mathrm{~g}$

117059.subject: Chemistry
117059.text: Which of the following pairs of elements exhibits almost identical atomic radii as a direct consequence of lanthanoid contraction?
117059.sol:
Due to lanthanoid contraction, the atomic radii of the elements of the 5d transition series are very similar to those of the corresponding elements of the 4d series. This effect is observed from Group 4 onwards because the filling of 4f orbitals occurs after Lanthanum ($\text{La}$, $Z=57$). Therefore, Niobium ($\text{Nb}$, 4d series) and Tantalum ($\text{Ta}$, 5d series) have almost identical atomic radii.

The pair $\text{Y}$ and $\text{La}$ (Group 3) does not show this effect as $\text{La}$ precedes the 4f series. $\text{Ti}$ and $\text{Zr}$ are 3d and 4d elements respectively, and their radii differ significantly as expected down a group. $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Mg}$ belong to the s-block and their similarity in size is due to a diagonal relationship, not lanthanoid contraction.

Answer: $\text{Nb}$ and $\text{Ta}$

121813.subject: Botany
121813.text: What type of leaves can be found in Pteridophytes?
121813.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves (Figure 3.3). These organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues. <mark>The leaves in pteridophytes are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns</mark>. The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones (Selaginella, Equisetum). The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells.

123560.subject: Botany
123560.text: During which phase of the cell cycle does the amount of DNA per cell double?
123560.sol: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G1, even after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. During the G2 phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues

123635.subject: Botany
123635.text: What is the precursor of the new cell wall in plant cells called?
123635.sol: Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells. In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis as a result of which multinucleate condition arises leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).

All the organelles responsible for the respective functions listed above collectively belong to which of the following cellular categories?
124366.sol:
The synthesis of steroidal hormones in animal cells is carried out by the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

The formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids is an important function of the Golgi apparatus.

The digestion of cellular waste is performed by lysosomes, which contain hydrolytic enzymes.

The endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and lysosomes (along with vacuoles) have coordinated functions and are therefore collectively considered as the endomembrane system.

Answer: Endomembrane system

125409.subject: Botany
125409.text: What component of chemiosmosis is responsible for creating the proton gradient?
125409.sol: Chemiosmosis requires a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient and ATP synthase. Energy is used to pump protons across a membrane, to create a gradient or a high concentration of protons within the thylakoid lumen. ATP synthase has a channel that allows diffusion of protons back across the membrane; this releases enough energy to activate ATP synthase enzyme that catalyses the formation of ATP. Along with the NADPH produced by the movement of electrons, the ATP will be used immediately in the biosynthetic reaction taking place in the stroma, responsible for fixing CO2 , and synthesis of sugars.

125839.subject: Botany
125839.text: What factors influence the period for which pollen grains remain viable?
125839.sol: When once they are shed, pollen grains have to land on the stigma before they lose viability if they have to bring about fertilisation. How long do you think the pollen grains retain viability? The period for which pollen grains remain viable is highly variable and to some extent depends on the prevailing temperature and humidity. In some cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release, and in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminoseae and Solanaceae, they maintain viability for months. You may have heard of storing semen/ sperms of many animals including humans for artificial insemination. It is possible to store pollen grains of a large number of species for years in liquid nitrogen (-1960C). Such stored pollen can be used as pollen banks, similar to seed banks, in crop breeding programmes.

125945.subject: Botany
125945.text: What becomes of the endosperm after free nuclei formation?
125945.sol: Endosperm development precedes embryo development. Why? The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly and forms a triploid endosperm tissue. The cells of this tissue are filled with reserve food materials and are used for the nutrition of the developing embryo. In the most common type of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give rise to free nuclei. This stage of endosperm development is called free-nuclear endosperm. Subsequently cell wall formation occurs and the endosperm becomes cellular. The number of free nuclei formed before cellularisation varies greatly. The coconut water from tender coconut that you are familiar with, is nothing but free-nuclear endosperm (made up of thousands of nuclei) and the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm.

127564.subject: Botany
127564.text: Which ecosystem is a shallow water body and simple example of all four basic components of an ecosystem?
127564.sol: To understand the ethos of an aquatic ecosystem let us take a small pond as an example. This is fairly a self-sustainable unit and rather simple example that explain even the complex interactions that exist in an aquatic ecosystem. A pond is a shallow water body in which all the above mentioned four basic components of an ecosystem are well exhibited. The abiotic component is the water with all the dissolved inorganic and organic substances and the rich soil deposit at the bottom of the pond. The solar input, the cycle of temperature, day-length and other climatic conditions regulate the rate of function of the entire pond. The autotrophic components include the phytoplankton, some algae and the floating, submerged and marginal plants found at the edges. The consumers are represented by the zooplankton, the free swimming and bottom dwelling forms. The decomposers are the fungi, bacteria and flagellates especially abundant in the bottom of the pond. This system performs all the functions of any ecosystem and of the biosphere as a whole, i.e., conversion of inorganic into organic material with the help of the radiant energy of the sun by the autotrophs; consumption of the autotrophs by heterotrophs; decomposition and mineralisation of the dead matter to release them back for reuse by the autotrophs, these event are repeated over and over again. There is unidirectional movement of energy towards the higher trophic levels and its dissipation and loss as heat to the environment.

127819.subject: Botany
127819.text:
Read the given statement and select the correct option to fill in the blanks.

In a lake ecosystem, the pyramid of energy is ___(A)___ and the pyramid of biomass is ___(B)___.
127819.sol:
The pyramid of energy is universally upright in all ecosystems because energy is lost as heat at each successive trophic level according to the 10 percent law. Therefore, (A) is Upright.

The pyramid of biomass in a lake or aquatic ecosystem is generally inverted because the standing crop biomass of the consumers (fishes, zooplankton) far exceeds that of the producers (phytoplankton) due to the producers' high turnover rate. Therefore, (B) is Inverted.

Answer: (A) Upright, (B) Inverted

129459.subject: Zoology
129459.text: What type of animals are referred to as ureotelic animals?
129459.sol: The process of excreting ammonia is Ammonotelism. Many bony fishes, aquatic amphibians and aquatic insects are ammonotelic in nature. Ammonia, as it is readily soluble, is generally excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or through gill surfaces (in fish) as ammonium ions. Kidneys do not play any significant role in its removal. Terrestrial adaptation necessitated the production of lesser toxic nitrogenous wastes like urea and uric acid for conservation of water. Mammals, many terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes mainly excrete urea and are called ureotelic animals. Ammonia produced by metabolism is converted into urea in the liver of these animals and released into the blood which is filtered and excreted out by the kidneys. Some amount of urea may be retained in the kidney matrix of some of these animals to maintain a desired osmolarity. Reptiles, birds, land snails and insects excrete nitrogenous wastes as uric acid in the form of pellet or paste with a minimum loss of water and are called uricotelic animals.

131436.subject: Zoology
131436.text: What is the structure of the DNA in nucleosomes?
131436.sol: In eukaryotes, this organization is much more complex. There is a set of positively charged, basic proteins called histones. A protein acquires charge depending upon the abundance of amino acids residues with charged side chains. Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine. Both the amino acid residues carry positive charges in their side chains. Histones are organized to form a unit of eight molecules called histone octamer. The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form a structure called nucleosome (Figure 5.4 a). A typical nucleosome contains 200 bp of DNA helix. Nucleosomes constitute the repeating unit of a structure in the nucleus called chromatin, threadlike stained (coloured) bodies seen in the nucleus. The nucleosomes in chromatin are seen as ‘beads-on-string’ structure when viewed under electron microscope

131464.subject: Zoology
131464.text: What was the initial belief about the genetic material before the work of Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty?
131464.sol: Prior to the work of Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty (1933-44), the genetic material was thought to be a protein. They worked to determine the biochemical nature of ‘transforming principle’ in Griffith's experiment. They purified biochemicals (proteins, DNA, RNA, etc.) from the heat-killed S cells to see which ones could transform live R cells into S cells. They discovered that DNA alone from S bacteria caused R bacteria to become transformed. They also discovered that protein-digesting enzymes (proteases) and RNA-digesting enzymes (RNases) did not affect transformation, so the transforming substance was not a protein or RNA. Digestion with DNase did inhibit transformation, suggesting that the DNA caused the transformation. They concluded that DNA is the hereditary material, but not all biologists were convinced
